resources.string: Settings map
Start with permissions, then choose how calls and contacts work. Account, synchronization, data, appearance, and technical options follow from general to detailed.
1. First-time setup
Make sure the app has the access it needs before changing its behavior.
2. Everyday work
Choose what happens during calls and how contacts are organized.
3. Account and shared data
Manage the company profile, server synchronization, and backups.
4. Personal preferences
Change language, text size, and the way the app looks.
5. Detailed and technical
Use these options only when you need diagnostics, tests, or fine control.
Permissions and readiness
Permissions and readiness\nAll permissions, Android roles, and an app readiness check
This is the first place to visit after installation. Enable missing access one item at a time. Android may open a separate system screen for some permissions and roles.
All permissions in one place

Allowed items are ready. Tap a missing item to enable it. Basic access is needed for calls, call history, contacts, and notifications; overlay, call screening, SMS, accessibility, and shared storage are optional and depend on the features you use.
Calls, popups, and history
Calls, popups, and history\nWhat appears during and after a call, and how the timeline is shown
Set the normal daily behavior in three steps: what happens during a call, which numbers trigger it, and how the Home timeline and History screen are displayed.
1. What happens during and after a call
Choose the popup type, the action after the call, and when temporary windows close.
2. Which numbers trigger the call experience
Choose known contacts, unknown numbers, and optional contact groups.
3. Home timeline and History screen
Control page size and how the phone call history is presented in the app.
Contacts and CRM
Contacts and CRM\nAndroid contacts, optional SMS integration, caller identification, and CRM links
Connect Relationship Manager with phone contacts and optional Android services. The permissions for these features are managed from “Permissions and readiness”.
1. Phone and SMS integrations
Optional Android roles for SMS and additional caller identification.
2. Contact links and synchronization
Create and maintain links between Relationship Manager records and Android contacts.
Company profile and access
Company profile and access\nLicense, company membership, invitations, and colleague access
Server synchronization
Server synchronization\nConnection status, pending notes, testing, and advanced server details
Data and backup
Data and backup\nWhere notes are stored, backup creation, and restore
Language, text, and appearance
Language, text, and appearance\nText size, app language, translations, and version information
Advanced settings and tests
Advanced settings and tests\nDiagnostics and test actions that are not needed in everyday use
